title: How Do You Make Bold Content That Stands Out in Your Industry? [Endless Customers Podcast Ep. 150]
article_body:
CSI Accounting & Payroll hired a videographer, named their competitors by name, and started asking the questions buyers were afraid to ask. Here's what happened.

Most accounting firms play it safe. They publish generic blog posts, avoid talking about competitors, and stay far away from anything that might feel uncomfortable. CSI Accounting & Payroll went the other direction.

In this episode, Bob Ruffolo sits down with Alex, the firm's marketing lead, and Jordan, their videographer, to talk about what it took to build a bold content culture inside an accounting firm and how they made an abstract, unglamorous topic like payroll data genuinely engaging on camera.

## Why most accounting content blends in

The team's core realization was that the content most firms produce is forgettable because it refuses to take a position. By being willing to go places competitors won't, including naming competitors directly and tackling the questions buyers are actually afraid to ask, CSI created content that stands out in a category known for being dry.

## How coaching changed the way they think about content

Coaching shifted CSI away from making content to impress peers and toward making content that genuinely helps buyers make decisions. Once that mindset clicked, the willingness to be bold followed naturally.

## Making payroll emotionally engaging on camera

The breakthrough was leading with the human stakes behind the topic, then letting real team members tell the story instead of reciting facts. The video Bob references in the episode lands because it puts a person and a real outcome at the center, not a list of features.

If you want to build a content culture that's willing to be bold in your own industry, [talk to the team at IMPACT about Endless Customers](https://www.impactplus.com/services/schedule-now).

title: What Happens When You Stop Chasing Traffic and Start Building Trust [Endless Customers Podcast Ep. 149]
article_body:
Dan Kerr and Adam Gardiner of AdjusterPro share how they hired a content manager and videographer in-house, and what changed once the right people were in the right seats.

AdjusterPro is the nation's leading provider of insurance adjuster licensing, exam prep, and continuing education courses. They were early to content years ago, but over the last decade they drifted: behind on video, behind on AI, with a marketing team Dan described as demoralized, confused, and ineffective despite having good people.

When Dan came back into the business at the start of 2025, he immediately recognized Endless Customers for what it was. "I said to Adam, this is EOS for sales and marketing."

## Why they committed to coaching instead of going it alone

Adam tried to implement Endless Customers on his own after reading the book, but knew he needed someone to execute and hold the team accountable. Dan returned full-time as Chief Revenue Officer, the integrator for the vision. Adding coaching on top was easy logic for a company already running on EOS: the system is the roadmap, and coaching is the outside accountability that keeps you moving through it.

## What the first few months actually looked like

Not smooth. The first six weeks to two months felt like being stuck in first gear: evaluating the team, figuring out who was in the right seat, and doing painful organizational work. The Alignment Day was clunky, and there was real fatigue and skepticism after multiple leadership turnovers. What turned it around was coaching, and eventually, results.

## How they found the right content manager

The person they needed was already on the team. When they posted the role internally and externally, a writer from the product development team applied, already screened as a culture fit, already understanding the product. She had a running start.

## What made them willing to tackle uncomfortable content

Once real content started getting produced, content that helped customers, the skeptics came around. It stopped being an idea and became something you could see working.

title: How Trailstone 2x'd Their Close Rate by Rebuilding Around Trust [Endless Customers Podcast Ep. 148]
article_body:
Trailstone Insurance turned negative reviews into video content, and it's paying off. Here's how they built trust by saying what most companies won't.

Mark Rodgers founded Trailstone Insurance in 2013 as a scratch agency out of Colorado, built on a core value of treating people the way you want to be treated. Today they're approaching 70 people across seven states, with a studio in their office, a full content production system, and a website they rebuilt from the ground up in 2024. When Marquece Cunningham joined as Marketing Director in 2025, one of the first things they did together was publish a video where they read their own one-star reviews out loud.

## Putting the company's core values into action

Mark came across They Ask, You Answer (now Endless Customers) on a 2020 road trip and got obsessed because it resonated with a core value: heart of a teacher. Getting the rest of the company there took about a year and a half. Today they hold quarterly Alignment Days, track who has read the book, and bake video willingness into hiring.

## What makes video so powerful in the insurance industry

There isn't much transparency in insurance, so Trailstone leaned into it. Their most transparent move was tackling one-star reviews face-to-face on camera, explaining what happened, where they messed up, and what they were doing to make it right. Instead of the ostrich effect, they addressed problems openly and built content no competitor in their market is making.

## How do you get the team comfortable on camera?

Video willingness doesn't just happen. Trailstone sends prospective employees a 90-second video assignment during hiring (about 40% of candidates won't do it, screening out people who won't get on camera). For current staff, they keep five to ten scripts loaded and bookable in the studio, and they share blooper reels to humanize the work.

## What happens when you rebuild your website around trust, instead of leads

Their old provider was all SEO and lead capture, and it didn't perform or reflect their values. Working with IMPACT coach Janet, they rebuilt 160+ pages on HubSpot starting from their values, not keywords. They launched with four website videos instead of the planned 34, because perfect is the enemy of growth.

## How website updates brought in more AI search traffic

After the rebuild, Janet produced a report showing AI-referred traffic, complete with the ChatGPT search string, the page clicked, and the form filled. Those AI-referred visitors are landing pre-qualified and closing at about double the previous rate, which is how the company 2x'd its close rate.

## Finding time to invest in what brings about the most change

Mark has introduced the system to about ten other agencies; most read the book, get excited, and stop. Trailstone avoided that trap by treating implementation like EOS: hire an implementer, commit to all of it, and get someone outside who can see what you're actually doing versus the stories you tell yourself.

## What's next for Trailstone Insurance?

The next phase is leaning into AI more deliberately to deliver pricing and answers before customers reach out, plus a longer-term vision of a content-driven media company serving insurance, mortgage, and loan officers under the same trust-first model.

If what Mark and Marquece are building resonates with you, [talk to the team at IMPACT about getting started with Endless Customers](https://www.impactplus.com/services/schedule-now).

title: How KangaRoof Got Early Wins Just 5 Weeks Into Endless Customers [Endless Customers Podcast Ep. 147]
article_body:
KangaRoof president Stacie Feller shares how her team got real wins just five weeks into Endless Customers, and what made the difference.

KangaRoof is a residential roofing company based in Round Rock, Texas, where Stacie has spent the last ten years building a team and culture focused on trust, education, and long-term customer relationships.

## What finally made the timing for Endless Customers right

Stacie had been aware of the approach but the timing finally aligned with where the business was, a point where she was ready to commit fully rather than dabble.

## How she got her team aligned before Alignment Day even happened

A big reason KangaRoof saw early wins is that Stacie did the cultural groundwork ahead of time. Her sales team is called roofing advisors, not salespeople, an intentional choice that already reflected the trust-and-education mindset Endless Customers is built on, so the team wasn't starting from scratch.

## The difference between "be people" and "do people"

Stacie distinguishes between people who simply are a certain way and people who actually do the work. Early wins came from a team willing to act, not just agree in principle.

## What she would tell another business owner thinking about this

Her advice was two parts. First, make sure it fits your culture; Endless Customers is built around trust and education, not shortcuts or pressure. Second, go all in: "If you're going to do it, jump in with both feet. Because otherwise it's not going to work." Half-effort that produces half-results is a commitment problem, not a program problem.

If where Stacie described resonates with your business, now is the time to [start a conversation with IMPACT](https://www.impactplus.com/services/schedule-now).

title: Why Video Might Be the Most Powerful Trust Tool in a High-Stakes Industry [Endless Customers Podcast Ep. 146]
article_body:
Marcos Navarro is the videographer at TMA Accounting, a small accounting firm that does accounting, taxes, and payroll all under one roof. In this episode, he shares how a full-time, in-house video function became one of the most powerful trust tools a high-stakes, detail-heavy business can build, earning trust with small business owners before the first sales conversation, and doing it with flair.

## Why every person has a story worth telling

Marcos's guiding belief is that every person has a story worth telling, and when a company learns to position itself as the guide inside the customer's story, the possibilities are endless. For an accounting firm, that means video isn't about showing off technical expertise, it's about helping the buyer feel understood.

## Building a YouTube strategy that earns trust before the first call

TMA's approach is to use video to answer the real questions small business owners have, so prospects arrive already trusting the firm. In a category where buyers are nervous about money, taxes, and compliance, seeing the real people behind the brand on camera lowers the stakes and builds confidence ahead of any sales conversation.

## Doing it with flair

What sets TMA apart is that the content isn't dry. Marcos brings personality and production value to topics most firms treat as boring, which is exactly what makes the videos memorable and trustworthy in a high-stakes industry.

title: How Equity Roofing's Pricing Page Drove a 58% Jump in Form Submissions [Endless Customers Podcast Ep. 145]
article_body:
Caitlin Vegas of Equity Roofing joins the show to break down how a single pricing page drove a 58% jump in form submissions, and what it takes to talk openly about cost in an industry that usually won't.

Most roofing companies dodge price. They make buyers call, sit through a pitch, and wait for a quote. Equity Roofing did the opposite: they published a pricing page that answers the cost questions homeowners are already asking, and the results showed up in their form submissions.

## Why pricing transparency works in roofing

Buyers are searching for cost before they ever pick up the phone. By addressing pricing openly, Equity Roofing met that intent head-on and earned trust, while competitors who hid their numbers lost those buyers to the back button.

## What the pricing page actually did

The page didn't just inform, it converted. Form submissions jumped 58% because visitors who got honest answers about cost were far more willing to raise their hand and start a conversation. Pricing transparency turned a page that most companies are afraid to publish into one of their strongest conversion assets.

## The lesson for any business afraid to talk about cost

The fear that publishing prices will scare buyers away is backwards. Buyers who can self-qualify on price arrive better prepared and more likely to convert, and Equity Roofing's 58% lift is the proof.

If you want to build a pricing page that converts in your own market, [talk to the team at IMPACT about Endless Customers](https://www.impactplus.com/services/schedule-now).

title: Are You Ready for Paid Ads? Here's How to Know [Endless Customers Podcast Ep. 144]
article_body:
Not sure if you're ready to run paid ads? In this episode, IMPACT paid social strategist Tanner Holman breaks down what your funnel, budget, creative, and tracking need to look like before you spend a dollar.

Paid ads can accelerate growth, but only when the fundamentals are in place. Running ads to a weak foundation just spends money faster. Tanner walks through the readiness checklist that determines whether paid media will pay off or burn cash.

## Is your funnel ready?

Ads drive traffic, but your website and offers have to convert that traffic. If your funnel leaks, paid media amplifies the leak. Make sure the pages you're sending people to are built to turn visitors into leads before you turn on ad spend.

## Do you have the budget to learn?

Paid platforms need data to optimize. A budget too small never gathers enough signal to find what works, so you need enough spend to get through a real learning phase rather than pulling the plug early.

## Is your creative trust-building?

The best-performing paid creative amplifies the same trust-building content that powers Endless Customers. Ads that educate and answer buyer questions outperform generic promotional creative.

## Can you track what's working?

Without proper tracking, you can't tell which ads, audiences, and offers are driving results, so you can't optimize. Tracking and attribution need to be in place before launch, not bolted on after.

If you want help deciding whether paid media is the right next move, [talk to the team at IMPACT](https://www.impactplus.com/services/schedule-now).
